incidents.victim: 100+ organizations (68% universities); University of Nottingham confirmed
incidents.vector: Exploited an unauthenticated remote-code-execution zero-day in Oracle PeopleSoft PeopleTools (CVE-2026-35273, CVSS 9.8) in the Environment Management Hub, then used MeshCentral C2, SSH credential spraying and zstd compression to exfiltrate data.
incidents.impact: Data stolen from 300+ PeopleSoft instances across 100+ orgs; University of Nottingham confirmed 40GB+ and 450,000+ student/alumni records taken. Extortion is active, with victims named on the group's leak site; Oracle disclosed the flaw June 10 without a patch.

incidents.victim: Phishing victims in 55 countries (Outsider network takedown)
incidents.vector: China-based 'Outsider' enterprise sold AI-assisted phishing kits and hosted infrastructure (from $88/week) used to spoof trusted brands and harvest card and bank credentials, defeating SMS/PIN/app verification.
incidents.impact: FBI, Google and Lumen seized core admin servers, domains and wallets; operation tied to ~$1.9B in losses and 3.9M stolen credit cards. Google filed a civil suit to dismantle remaining infrastructure.

incidents.vector: Ukrainian national Oleksii Lytvynenko developed malware used in Conti ransomware attacks (2021-2022) that encrypted systems and stole data for extortion.
incidents.impact: Lytvynenko pleaded guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and faces up to 20 years; Conti extorted $150M+ from 1,000+ victims globally, including a Tennessee sheriff's department, EMS and police. Sentencing set for Sept. 10.

incidents.vector: Suspected Russian state-linked actors compromised the lawmaker's Signal messaging account.
incidents.impact: FBI notified Bacon — a vocal Ukraine supporter and Kremlin critic — that his encrypted Signal account was breached, raising concerns over access to sensitive communications.

incidents.vector: Unauthorized access to a Thai government agency managing healthcare entitlements; method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Personal information of more than 67 million Thai citizens allegedly stolen, with portions posted to online black markets. The Thai government has opened an investigation.

incidents.vector: A 2025 breach traced back to a Chinese software engineer who has since left South Korea, indicating likely insider access to customer data.
incidents.impact: South Korea fined Coupang $409M (about 1.7% of 2025 sales) over the breach that exposed the data of 34 million citizens. Coupang says it will appeal.

incidents.victim: Jamaica Ministry of Health / National Health Fund
incidents.vector: Threat actor claims to have stolen data and contacted the National Health Fund demanding payment to prevent its release.
incidents.impact: The Jamaican health ministry is being extorted; the government says it is still investigating whether a breach actually occurred.

incidents.vector: Cyberattack of undisclosed type disrupted operational systems at the start of the sugarcane crushing season.
incidents.impact: Australia's second-largest sugar producer paused cane haulage and milling at two Mackay-region mills, halting operations during peak season.

incidents.vector: Iranian-linked hacktivists breached the news outlet's website, deleting articles and disrupting online broadcasts.
incidents.impact: The Handala persona claimed the attack, took down content and broadcasts, and threatened to dox and harm the agency's employees.

incidents.vector: Spear-phishing social-engineering campaign luring WhatsApp users to click malicious links to external sites; NSO also created WhatsApp test accounts and groups.
incidents.impact: Meta says it disrupted the campaign and is asking a US court to hold NSO in contempt for violating an October 2025 injunction barring it from targeting WhatsApp.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; exploitation reportedly dates back to at least April.
incidents.impact: ServiceNow quietly patched the flaw and notified affected customers; incidents mainly impacted customers on its Australia platform release.

incidents.victim: US law firms (incl. Weil, Gotshal & Manges)
incidents.vector: Voice-phishing and IT-helpdesk impersonation tricked staff into screen-sharing and installing RMM tools; in some cases actors physically entered offices posing as IT technicians to exfiltrate data via USB.
incidents.impact: Dozens of US legal, financial and professional-services firms hit with rapid data-theft extortion, often within a single business day. Weil, Gotshal & Manges reportedly paid an estimated $20M to prevent release of stolen client data.

incidents.vector: Attackers accessed the university's CareerConnect careers portal in late May and stole stored records.
incidents.impact: Data of alumni, research staff and employers using the platform was stolen; the university disclosed the breach.
